original.prompt: Consider the following statements about the interim India-US trade pact of February 2026:
items: Under the pact, Washington offered an 18% tariff track for Indian exports.
The pact was unwound by a Supreme Court ruling in May 2026.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
original.explain: The Supreme Court ruling that unwound the pact came in March 2026, weeks after it was struck, not in May. In return for the 18% track, India was to lower trade barriers and buy more American goods. A temporary 10% tariff was due to lapse on 24 July 2026.
original.source: The interim pact in February involved India lowering trade barriers and buying more American goods, while Washington offered an 18% tariff track for Indian exports (we covered it here).

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about the interim India-US trade pact of February 2026:
items: Under the pact, Washington offered a 10% tariff track for Indian exports.
The pact was unwound by a Supreme Court ruling in May 2026.
rewritten.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
rewritten.explain: Both statements are wrong: Washington offered an 18% tariff track, not 10%, and the Supreme Court ruling that unwound the pact came in March 2026, not May. The 10% figure is the temporary tariff now in place, which lapses on 24 July 2026.
rewritten.source: The Supreme Court ruling in March unwound it weeks later, and a temporary 10% tariff now lapses on July 24.
